artifacts.summary: Research on converting README-date, C20-citation, and C16-env_linter-root advisory findings into pinned, regression-blocking baselines, reusing the repo's existing nolints.json/c20-declaration-baseline.txt/warning-budget.txt ratchet model.

memory_candidates.content: This repo's canonical ratchet-baseline pattern (nolints.json, c20-declaration-baseline.txt, warning-budget.txt) is deliberately keyed by stable item identity (declaration name, citer|target|names triple, or path|linter) rather than a bare aggregate count -- warning-budget.py's own docstring explains an aggregate count cannot distinguish 'one fixed, one new, net unchanged' from 'no new finding.' When adding a new enforceable baseline in a Lean/Mathlib-style repo, prefer per-item keying and reuse an existing mechanism (e.g. nolints.json, read unconditionally by runLinter.lean regardless of module argument) over inventing a parallel file.

A check-module-invariants.sh-style script's RUN_BUILD-gated blocks can be invisible to CI even when the script itself is wired into CI, if CI calls it with --no-build. Before assuming 'flip ENFORCE_X to 1' adds CI coverage, verify which flag/path CI actually exercises (grep the workflow for --no-build and for separate build/lint steps such as lean-action's lint:true) -- local full-mode enforcement and CI enforcement can diverge silently.
